analysis.title: US Market Intelligence - Afternoon Briefing
key_insights: Stocks closed higher on Nov 4 after the US midterms: SPX +1.6%, NDX +0.9%, RTY +1.6%. WTI fell 7.86% to $88.54, gold rose 3.39% to $4,063, the 10Y yield was 4.886% and VIX 16.74.
Investors rotated from AI, memory and semis into Mag7 and software. Part of the move was short covering: JPM's Crowded Shorts basket rose 3.2%.

Europe closed sharply higher (SX5E +2.0%, DAX +2.2%, UKX +1.8%). Banks and retail outperformed, energy and tech lagged, and momentum unwound. UK, French and Italian 10-year yields fell more than 10bp as oil dropped.

ISM services was consistent with strong growth. The business activity index fell 2.7 points to 53.8, new orders fell 3.9 points to 55.9, prices paid eased to 73.0 and employment rose 1.3 points to 51.4. JPM US Market Intel read it as growth stable with inflation edging down, driven by tariffs and energy costs.
ADP private payrolls were +86k in October, the same as revised September, with a three-month average of 69k. JPM's forecast for Friday's BLS payrolls is 75k for both private and total employment.
Ron Adler said the election cleared one of two hurdles and the VIX reflects the relief. The margin of victory was more surprising than the result, and Trump's conciliatory tone was a positive signal.

Mike Feroli: the Democratic Senate reduces risks to Fed independence. The administration must now pick a replacement for Powell's governor seat (term ends January 2028) that Senate Democrats will accept, or leave it vacant. A successful removal of Governor Cook would no longer open a seat for an administration ally.

Equity desks saw large-cap quality with access to financing and compute (AMZN, GOOGL, MSFT) bid, and second-tier AI names reliant on capital raises (CRWV, NBIS) weak. Internet outperformed: KWEB +5% against IGV +1%.
Consumer desks said the rally was driven by short covering and macro, not real-money buying. Price action is better than sponsorship.
Rates desk: Treasuries 2-4bp richer with a bull steepening curve. Treasury refunding was expected to leave coupon auction sizes unchanged. JPM stays in 10s30s steepeners.
Equity derivatives: JPM's AI Leaders, AI Infra Winners and AI Bottleneck baskets moved about -5 standard deviations relative to QQQ. Tech vol is rising on a sell-off for the first time this year.

JPM Credit Research expects ballot measures restricting data centers (about 45 across 13 states) to slow data center development from 2028 onward, with no material change to 2027 capital plans. Existing built or permitted assets gain value. IPPs and behind-the-meter power providers face near-term weakness.
Nikos: hedge fund de-risking in October is likely over, which is a better positioning backdrop for equities and AI stocks into year-end. Hedge funds could rebuild AI exposure from end-November.

JPM US Market Intel stays Tactically Bullish. Its reasons: a near-term rebound after a Friday flush (NDX within 6% of its high and down 3.5% or more averages about +3% the next week), data that should ease recession fears, a limited oil upside from a Middle East re-escalation, and positive November and post-midterm seasonality.

The Monetization Menu (Nov 2) favors a barbell of Tech and Cyclicals, weighted toward Cyclicals, with Consumers and Financials working if the curve steepens, and Europe catching a bid if US/Iran move toward a deal.

market_movers.rationale: TMT desk saw large moves higher in AMZN, GOOGL and MSFT as owners of compute with clear access to financing.
TMT desk saw demand in META versus selling in GOOGL, but large moves higher in the hyperscalers after the election.
Hyperscalers rose on the view that a slower data center build helps companies with existing capacity.
Second-tier AI players that depend on continuous capital raises were weak early.
Second-tier AI player dependent on capital raises, weak early.
The TMT desk thinks the move is largely short covering. Lower capex would ease input cost pressure and Apple's margin pressure.
Well off pre-market lows despite a disappointing guide that many will view as conservative. Little impact on SNOW.
Up 12% in an Internet rally, which the TMT desk calls the anti-'anti AI' trade.
Consumer desks saw genuine long demand in LTH, along with DAL, WYNN and KDP.
Hedge fund demand in Medicaid names CNC and MOH.
Hedge fund demand in Medicaid names CNC and MOH.

sector_views.rationale: JPM likes broad-based Tech exposure but says the day is not an all clear for AI. It prefers large caps and a barbell with Cyclicals.
Broadening favors Cyclicals over Defensives, especially Consumers and Financials if the curve steepens.
Better near-term expression of Value, lighter positioning, and a catch-up if US/Iran move toward a deal.
JPM Credit expects weakness, especially for names with Texas, Ohio, Pennsylvania and Georgia exposure.
Desks see price action ahead of real-money sponsorship, and expect hedge funds to look at the group as Q1 shorts again into December.

earnings_insights: DDOG (reported 11/4 before the open): the TMT desk called the guide disappointing but likely to be viewed as conservative. The stock recovered well off its pre-market lows.

Earnings reporting Nov 5 before the open includes AAP, APD, BDX, CAH, CI, CMI, COP, KMB, PH, RL, SO, TPR and ZTS. After the close it includes ABNB, AFRM, AKAM, AXON, DKNG, DVN, EOG, IONQ, LYFT, LYV, MCHP, NET and WYNN.
JPM said the earnings season has been solid, as a tailwind cited by Ron Adler (no figures given).

crypto_views: Nikos: the Binance hack exposed infrastructure risks, but crypto markets have remained relatively resilient.

trade_ideas.description: Long ACA Subsidies basket (JPUXACA) and short Government Contractors basket (JPUXFEDB)
trade_ideas.rationale: Post-election conviction trades responding as intended and may still be in the early innings.

trade_ideas.description: Barbell of Tech and Cyclicals, heavier on Cyclicals
trade_ideas.rationale: Broadening can continue and the market may resemble the first two months of the year, with less Energy appreciation and less Tech downside.
Strategy stays in the position, and an unchanged refunding could push the curve steeper if the market expected something more active.

trade_ideas.description: Favor Europe equities as an expression of Value
trade_ideas.rationale: Lighter positioning and a possible US/Iran deal.

risk_factors: Re-escalation in the Middle East is the biggest non-AI risk.
AI capex decline and data center restrictions could cut capex and GDP growth, and cause hyperscaler layoffs.
Tariffs and energy costs keep inflation pressure elevated.
Consumer rally may be short-covering driven and could reverse into December and Q1.
Long-duration real money investors could limit the fall in yields.
Weekend headlines on AI capital raising, circular financing and legal issues may give investors pause.
vol_and_positioning: VIX at 16.74, with the relief tied to the election being cleared.
JPM equity derivatives saw vols rising across many Tech corners, the first time this year on a tech sell-off.
The Short Interest factor moved 4 sigma while the Squeeze Index barely moved, so the move is short covering in rate-sensitive names, not a broad squeeze.
Hedge funds are shorting moves higher in healthcare and moves lower in tech. Nobody is leaning heavily short in AI, though investors are more open to the idea.
Consumer retail index positioning is at the 64th percentile on a one-year lookback, lower in footwear and global brands.
JPM volumes were tracking -16% early with a mild sell skew. Long-only volumes were 60% above hedge fund volumes.
JPM's Crowded Shorts basket was +3.2% and crowded Consumer and HC longs rose 4.2 and 2.0 standard deviations.
geopolitical: US midterms: Democrats took the House and Senate, which markets read as a check on Trump's agenda.
Iran war: Schumer and Jeffries pledged to end it. JPM expects lower odds of significant escalation after the midterms, and oil fell.
A WSJ report on Iranian damage to US regional bases, with depleted munitions, points to limited scope for another wave of attacks and more diplomacy.
Iran's guerrilla tactics around the Strait of Hormuz (WSJ news link).
US and China agreed to extend the trade truce through January 20, 2027.
Jeffries said the House would pass a bill to stop Trump's tariffs.

tension_points.bull_case: JPM US Market Intel and Nikos see hedge fund de-risking behind us, mega tech and hyperscalers benefiting from a slower build, and year-end seasonality supporting a rebound.
tension_points.bear_case: JPM derivatives notes AI baskets moved about -5 standard deviations against QQQ and tech vol is rising. Data center ballot measures could slow 2028 and later capex.
tension_points.what_invalidates: JPM derivatives says it is hard to see the market rally into year-end without AI participating.

tension_points.bull_case: Macro tailwinds (midterms, lower oil and yields) lifted consumer indices 2-3 standard deviations, and the holiday may carry through Black Friday and Cyber Monday.
tension_points.bear_case: Consumer desks say flows are not real-money buying. Discretionary demand is mostly hedge fund short covering and hedge funds may revisit the group as Q1 shorts in December.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Evidence of broader real-money participation would change the desk's view that the rally is factor-driven.

tension_points.bull_case: Democratic control checks fiscal expansion, giving duration an initial bid and bull steepening.
tension_points.bear_case: Services inflation is elevated, labor data firm, and an unchanged refunding announcement could push the curve steeper if the market expected activism.
